breakfast.name: Medialunas (Argentine Croissants)
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm milk with a pinch of sugar
Mix flour, sugar, salt; add yeast mixture and eggs
Knead until smooth, refrigerate 30 min
Roll out, layer cold butter, fold in thirds three times, chilling between folds
Roll final dough, cut triangles, roll into crescent shapes
Rise 1 hour until puffy
Brush with egg wash
Bake at 200°C for 15-18 min until deeply golden
Brush immediately with warm sugar syrup for glaze
breakfast.description: Argentina's answer to the croissant — smaller, sweeter, and glazed. Eaten by the dozen at every bakery.

breakfast.name: Mate con Tostadas
instructions: Fill mate gourd two-thirds with yerba
Tilt gourd so yerba sits on one side
Insert bombilla into the lower part
Pour warm water over the lower side, let absorb
Continue pouring water to drink through bombilla
Toast bread, spread with butter and dulce de leche
breakfast.description: The true Argentine breakfast — bitter mate sipped through a metal straw alongside toast with dulce de leche.

breakfast.name: Tortilla de Papa (Potato Omelette)
instructions: Fry potato slices in olive oil until tender, not crispy
Add onion slices, cook until soft
Beat eggs with salt and pepper
Drain potatoes, mix into eggs
Pour into oiled skillet, cook on medium-low until edges set
Flip using a plate, cook other side 3 min
Slide onto plate, cut into wedges
breakfast.description: Argentine-style Spanish tortilla — thick, golden, eaten at any hour.

lunch.name: Empanadas Salteñas
ingredients: Dough: 500g flour, 100g beef fat, 1 tsp salt, warm water
Filling: 500g beef (diced small), 2 onions, 2 hard-boiled eggs, green olives, cumin, paprika, chili flakes, green onion
instructions: Make dough: mix flour, salt, melted beef fat, add water until pliable, rest 30 min
Sauté onions in beef fat, add paprika, cumin, chili
Add diced beef, cook until just done — filling should be juicy, not dry
Cool filling, add chopped egg and olives
Roll dough circles, fill each generously
Fold in half, crimp edges with repulgue (decorative rope fold)
Bake at 220°C for 15-18 min until golden
lunch.description: Salta-style baked empanadas — the juiciest in Argentina, with beef fat dough and a signature crimped edge.

lunch.name: Milanesa a la Napolitana
instructions: Pound beef thin, season with salt
Dip in egg, then breadcrumbs
Fry until golden on both sides
Place on baking sheet
Top each with tomato sauce, ham, mozzarella, oregano
Broil until cheese melts and bubbles
Serve with fries or salad
lunch.description: Breaded beef topped with ham, tomato, and melted cheese — invented in Buenos Aires, not Naples.

lunch.name: Locro (Northwest Stew)
ingredients: Quiquirimichi: red pepper flakes, cumin, oil, green onion
instructions: Cook soaked corn and beans in large pot with plenty of water, 1 hour
Add beef and pork ribs, cook 1 more hour
Add squash, chorizo, onions, bay leaf
Simmer 30 min — squash should dissolve into the broth, thickening it
Season with cumin, paprika, salt
Make quiquirimichi: fry green onion in oil, add pepper flakes and cumin
Serve in deep bowls with quiquirimichi spooned on top
lunch.description: Argentina's national stew — served on May 25th (Revolution Day) and through winter. Thick, ancient, and warming.

dinner.name: Asado Completo (Full Argentine BBQ)
ingredients: Chimichurri: parsley, oregano, garlic, red pepper flakes, olive oil, red wine vinegar
instructions: Build fire to one side of the grill, let burn down to white coals
Salt meat generously with coarse salt only
Place ribs bone-side down far from coals for slow cooking
Add vacío fat-side down
Grill chorizos and morcillas closer to heat, 15 min
Ribs take 90 min+ over low heat — never rush
Flip vacío once after 40 min, cook 20 more min
Rest all meats 10 min before cutting
Slice against the grain, serve with chimichurri
dinner.description: The sacred Argentine ritual — hours of slow-grilling over wood coals. The asador tends the fire; guests wait patiently.

dinner.name: Carbonada Criolla
instructions: Brown beef in oil
Sauté onion and tomatoes
Add paprika, bay leaf, broth
Add potatoes and sweet potato
Simmer 30 min
Add corn rounds and peach halves
Cook 15 more min until everything is tender
The peaches should be soft but hold their shape
dinner.description: Sweet-savory beef stew with peaches and corn — a colonial-era dish from the Pampas.

dinner.name: Matambre Arrollado (Stuffed Rolled Flank)
instructions: Butterfly matambre if needed, pound thin
Marinate in vinegar, garlic, oregano, salt, pepper overnight
Lay flat, layer spinach, roasted pepper strips, carrot sticks
Place whole hard-boiled eggs in a line down the center
Roll tightly, tie with twine at 3cm intervals
Wrap in foil, simmer in salted water 90 min
Cool under weight in fridge overnight
Slice into pinwheel rounds, serve cold
dinner.description: Rolled stuffed flank steak — sliced cold to reveal a colorful spiral. A celebration centerpiece.

snacks.name: Choripán
ingredients: Chimichurri: flat-leaf parsley, garlic, oregano, red pepper flakes, olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt
instructions: Butterfly chorizos lengthwise (don't cut through)
Grill cut-side down first until charred, then flip
Make chimichurri: finely chop parsley, garlic; mix with oregano, pepper flakes, oil, vinegar, salt
Split rolls, place chorizo inside
Spoon chimichurri generously over
snacks.description: Grilled chorizo sandwich with chimichurri — Argentina's king of street food, sold at every fútbol match.

snacks.name: Provoleta
instructions: Place cheese rounds on hot grill or cast iron
Cook without moving until bottom is golden and crispy, 4-5 min
Flip carefully, cook 2 more min until melty inside
Sprinkle with oregano and pepper flakes
Drizzle with olive oil, eat immediately with bread
snacks.description: Grilled provolone — bubbly and golden, the opening act of every asado.

snacks.name: Fugazzeta (Cheese-Stuffed Onion Pizza)
ingredients: Dough: 500g flour, 7g yeast, 300ml warm water, 2 tbsp olive oil, salt
Topping: 3 large onions (sliced thin into rings), oregano, olive oil
instructions: Make dough, rise 1 hour
Divide in half — roll bottom crust into greased round pan
Cover with mozzarella cheese
Roll second crust on top, press edges to seal
Pile sliced onions thick on top — they should completely cover the surface
Drizzle olive oil, sprinkle oregano
Bake at 220°C for 20-25 min until golden and onions are soft
The cheese melts inside, creating a stretchy hidden layer
snacks.description: Buenos Aires' signature pizza — cheese hidden between two crusts, buried under a mountain of onions. Went viral when food creators discovered you can't see the cheese until you cut it. A BA pizzería classic since the 1930s.

desserts.name: Alfajores de Maicena
instructions: Cream butter with powdered sugar
Add egg yolks, vanilla, lemon zest
Sift cornstarch, flour, baking powder; fold in
Roll dough 5mm thick, cut rounds
Bake at 160°C for 10-12 min — they should NOT brown, stay pale
Cool completely
Sandwich with generous dulce de leche
Roll edges in shredded coconut
desserts.description: Argentina's most beloved cookie — delicate cornstarch shortbread sandwiching dulce de leche, rolled in coconut.

desserts.name: Dulce de Leche Flan
ingredients: Custard: 6 eggs, 500ml whole milk, 200g dulce de leche, 1 tsp vanilla
instructions: Melt sugar in flan mold until amber caramel, swirl to coat
Warm milk, whisk in dulce de leche until dissolved
Beat eggs, temper with warm milk mixture
Strain into caramelized mold
Place in water bath, bake at 160°C for 55-60 min
Jiggle test: center should wobble like jelly, not liquid
Cool, refrigerate overnight
Unmold by running knife around edge, invert onto plate — caramel cascades down
desserts.description: Flan with dulce de leche stirred into the custard and more pooled on top. Sunday lunch dessert across Argentina.

desserts.name: Chocotorta (No-Bake Chocolate Biscuit Cake)
instructions: Mix cream cheese with dulce de leche until smooth
Briefly dip chocolinas in coffee — just a second, don't soak them
Layer in a rectangular dish: coffee-dipped cookies, dulce de leche cream, repeat
Top layer should be cream
Refrigerate overnight — the cookies soften and meld together
Dust with cocoa powder before serving
Cut into squares
desserts.description: Argentina's viral birthday cake — no oven needed, no baking skill required. Chocolinas cookies layered with dulce de leche and cream cheese. Went globally viral on TikTok. Every Argentine child grows up eating this at birthday parties.

drinks.name: Mate
instructions: Fill gourd two-thirds full with yerba mate
Cover opening, flip upside down and shake gently to bring fine dust to top
Tilt so yerba sits at an angle
Pour a small amount of cool water on the lower side, let absorb
Insert bombilla into the wet side
Pour hot water (never boiling) over the lower side
Drink through bombilla until you hear slurping
Refill with hot water, pass to next person in the circle
drinks.description: More than a drink — a social ritual. The cebador (server) prepares and refills; everyone shares one gourd. Argentina's national beverage.

drinks.name: Fernet con Coca
instructions: Fill tall glass with ice
Pour Fernet Branca over ice
Top slowly with Coca-Cola
Stir gently once — don't kill the fizz
Drink ratio is personal: Córdoba pours it stronger
drinks.description: The bittersweet drink of Argentine nightlife — practically the national cocktail, especially in Córdoba.
